subject: memoise doesn't work as expected when deployed to shiny server, works fine locally

messages.author: ce4116ba0e74c394
messages.subject: memoise doesn't work as expected when deployed to shiny server, works fine locally
parts:
Hi,

I've been trying to use memoise with shiny server, but even when I declare near the top of an app.R outside of server.R , it seems not to cache when deployed to shiny server? 

mSPARQL <- memoise(SPARQL, ~timeout(3600))  

When working with shiny on my local box, the behavior is fine it caches the data with no problem. I did see another reference in the groups here, but it did not work for me?
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/GPdLbZEN45s

Any thoughts suggestions? 

Omar

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: memoise doesn't work as expected when deployed to shiny server, works fine locally
parts:
Shiny Server aggressively shuts down R processes when they are not in use, and starts up new ones when they are needed. Memoise only applies within a single process.

You can use the app_idle_timeout directive in your shiny-server.conf to customize this behavior (the default is to shut down after 5 seconds of having no connected clients, or possibly 20 seconds depending on how the last client exits, I think).

messages.subject: Re: memoise doesn't work as expected when deployed to shiny server, works fine locally
parts:
Hi,

I did try increasing the app_idle_timeout directive, still no avail. I also tried filesystem_cache from the dev version, and the interesting part, was I could get it to write to the file - but reasons unknown each iteration it would treat the cache as not being held and would not recognize the cache even if existed. 

I've also read articles about persisting data on the server in terms of writing files, but believe that could become problematic at best if scaled up to many users.

I decided to try a different approach and cache outside of shiny. 

I had good luck staging an redis server as a cache, and believe this worked fine with the https://github.com/bwlewis/rredis it just seems complicated to solve a problem of caching. 

Are there any other suggestions to perform caching? Or tests / troubleshooting suggestions, I could try to see where memoise isn't holding the details. Otherwise, I think I'll continue working with rredis, which may in fact be more scaleable in the end. 

thanks again for the help!
Omar
